verdict.rationale: Sentry publishes self-hosted source and docs describe running 'all of Sentry on your own server, without paying anything' (sentry-docs-11/26/37/39), and one HN commenter praises its 'fully open source nature' for letting them read the code (sentry-comm-1). However, another community comment explicitly calls a licensing change 'disappointing' and says they 'refuse to rely on closed-source software' now (sentry-comm-3), reflecting Sentry's shift to the non-OSI Business Source License (BSL) rather than a permissive open-source license — a concrete counter-example to the 'open license' claim. missing for 10: an official statement of the current license terms in the evidence pack, clarification of BSL conversion-to-Apache timeline, and independent confirmation that source is fully inspectable under an OSI-approved license.
